title: Choosing a Digital Honours Board for Your Sports Club
description: Compare the records, search, sharing, export and display requirements that matter when choosing digital honours board software for a sports club.
html:
A digital honours board should help members find the history that matters to them. Before choosing software or buying a screen, establish where your winner records are, how complete they are and who will check them. A polished display cannot resolve an uncertain name on an old trophy.

This is a buyer’s checklist from Trophy Guru, a provider of trophy digitisation and online honours boards. It is not an independent ranking or a claim that we have tested every supplier.

Start with the records, then choose the presentation

Some clubs already have a checked spreadsheet of competition winners. Others have decades of names spread across silver cups, wooden boards, minute books and individual volunteers’ files. These clubs have different first jobs. The former can concentrate on presentation; the latter needs a capture and review process before publication.

Choose one representative trophy and follow it through the proposed system. Can you check a name against the source photograph? Can you correct a year? What happens when an entry remains uncertain? Ask to see those steps before judging the finished display.

Decide how members will use the board

  • By year: a member wants to see who won the club’s competitions in a particular season.
  • By trophy: a past captain wants to follow the history of one cup.
  • By person: a member wants to find the honours associated with a name.
  • On a phone: a visitor wants to explore the archive away from the clubhouse.

A static slide can suit a simple display of recent winners. A searchable archive serves a different need: finding individual records across many competitions and seasons. Decide which tasks matter to your members and test them in a demonstration.

Questions to ask each supplier

  1. What format must our existing records be in, and who does the initial data entry?
  2. Can we correct a record and keep the source evidence available to our reviewers?
  3. Can members search the published history, and which fields can they search?
  4. Can we export our records in a usable format if our plans change?
  5. Who controls publication, and can we withdraw the board?
  6. What is included in the price: software, hosting, transcription, hardware, installation and support?
  7. If we need a clubhouse screen, can we test the exact device and browser before purchasing?

Where Trophy Guru fits

Trophy Guru helps clubs recover winner names and years from photographs of trophies and supporting records. The proposed readings remain editable and require human review. Confirmed records can be shared as an electronic honours board, with views by year, trophy and person. CSV export gives the club a separate copy of its recorded information.

The offer covers an archive and online board. It does not include screen hardware or on-site installation. Do not assume that an arbitrary smart TV or streaming stick will provide the browsing experience your club needs; test your intended equipment.

Compare the cost of a realistic pilot

Trophy Guru’s first trophy is free, with up to 12 saved photographs and no payment card required. Additional credits cost £7.50 for one trophy, £60 for ten or £250 for fifty, including VAT. Core archive credits are a one-time purchase and do not expire. Optional Intelligent Golf integration has a separate annual charge and availability conditions; check the full current pricing.

Include the time needed to gather photographs and review exceptions in your project estimate. We do not promise that a whole cabinet can be completed in a weekend. Use the committee project plan to estimate the work from your own pilot, then explore the public demonstration before creating an account.
